config.defaultModel.description: Fallback model for new threads: used only for a provider route that has no entry in `brotherwhale.modelByProvider` and no model in its own runtime catalog.
config.defaultMode.description: Default mode for new threads: agent (Act), plan, or operate
config.defaultPermissionPosture.descript: Default permission posture for new threads: ask, auto_review, or full_access (the TUI's Ask / Auto-Review / Full Access)
config.reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort level (auto, off, low, medium, high, max)
config.autoApprove.description: Legacy fallback: auto-approve tool calls. Prefer the Full Access permission posture, which already implies auto-approval.
config.costCurrency.description: Currency for cost display: auto follows the interface language (Chinese → CNY, otherwise USD), or force USD/CNY. Amounts come from the TUI runtime's provider-published pricing; when no native CNY price exists the display falls back to USD (same as the TUI).
config.backgroundThreadNotifications.des: Show a VS Code notification when a background thread needs your approval or input (each fires once per attention episode; the Threads rail badge always stays live).
config.modelByProvider.description: The model each provider route's new threads start from, keyed by the route's id (`model_provider_id` when it has one). `/model` and the provider picker write here, so choosing a model on one route no longer changes what another route's new threads use. `brotherwhale.defaultModel` remains the fallback for a route with no entry here.
